question: How do BFS and DFS work on graphs and grids?

scenes.sub: BFS spreads in rings. DFS dives deep, then backs up.
scenes.say: Breadth first and depth first search visit every cell of a grid or graph. They differ only in what order they visit.

scenes.head: Two ways to explore

items.label: BFS: ripples in a pond
items.sub: uses a queue (first in, first out)

items.label: DFS: a maze
items.text: follow one tunnel to its end

scenes.say: Two ways to explore. Breadth first search is like ripples in a pond: it reaches the nearest cells first, using a queue. Depth first search is like a maze: follow one tunnel to its end, then back up. Use BFS for fewest steps. Use DFS to ask how many areas, or whether something exists.

scenes.head: BFS on a grid: fewest steps from top left to bottom right
scenes.say: A grid. Dots are floor, hash is wall. Start top left, exit bottom right. Fewest steps? Breadth first search spreads in rings. Layer zero is the start. Layer one is its neighbor. Layer two. Layer three has two cells. The wall blocks the way down, so only one route continues. Layer four. Layer five reaches the exit, so the answer is five. Layer six fills the corner, but we're done.

scenes.head: BFS code: a queue and a distance table
scenes.say: The code. A queue holds cells waiting to be visited, first in first out. The distance table starts at minus one, which also means not visited. Pop a cell. Try its four neighbors. Skip cells outside, walls, and visited ones. Otherwise set the distance one more and queue it. Each cell enters once, so it's O of rows times columns.

scenes.head: DFS code: count islands by sinking them
scenes.say: Depth first search goes as deep as possible, then backs up. Count islands of ones. Scan the grid. At each unvisited one, count an island, and call dfs. It sinks the whole island by turning ones to zeros, recursing in four directions. O of cells. Warning: a million cells can overflow the recursion stack. Use BFS or an explicit stack.

scenes.head: In the interview
rows: BFS or DFS for shortest path?
BFS if unweighted. Weighted needs Dijkstra.
O of V plus E. On a grid, O of rows times columns.
Use an explicit stack, or BFS.
Marking visited when popping, not when pushing.
scenes.say: BFS or DFS for shortest path? BFS if unweighted. Complexity? O of V plus E. Deep recursion crashes? Use an explicit stack, or BFS. Common mistake: marking visited when popping, not when pushing, so cells enter the queue many times.

lines: BFS uses a queue and finds fewest steps.
DFS uses a stack or recursion, and finds areas and cycles.
Both are O(V + E). Mark visited when you push.
scenes.say: BFS uses a queue and finds the fewest steps. DFS uses a stack or recursion, and finds areas and cycles. Both are O of V plus E. Mark a cell visited when you push it.
